pages.title: Viaje al centro de un agujero negro - NASA
pages.description: Bienvenidos a un vuelo imaginario con destino a un agujero negro. Con el astrofísico de la NASA Javier García como piloto, nos embarcamos en una odisea espacial donde el tiempo se dilata, la luz se curva, y las leyes de la física colapsan. Descubre cómo la NASA detecta y estudia estos fascinantes objetos cósmicos, qué es la espaguetización, y qué misterios aguardan más allá del horizonte de eventos. Advertencia: este es un viaje solo de ida. ¿Te atreves a sumarte a la aventura?

Vibe Coding Explained: How AI Is Changing the Way You Build Software Written by Coursera Staff • Updated on Oct 2, 2026 Explore how AI is transforming software development and how you can use vibe coding to your advantage. Key takeaways Vibe coding is an AI-assisted approach to software development that uses natural language prompts to generate code with minimal manual coding. Vibe code tools include ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, Bolt, Bubble, or Glide. Vibe coding works by entering your instructions for what you want to build into specialized AI tools that generate the code for you to review and refine in an ongoing conversational loop. Users typically choose one of two vibe coding approaches: one that relies heavily on AI for all coding and another that fosters more human-AI collaboration with more extensive expert oversight. Learn more about what vibe coding is, how it works, its benefits and potential challenges, and how you can begin vibe coding, which is emerging as a new role requiring skills such as prompt engineering and AI collaboration. Refine your ability to interact with AI by enrolling in Vanderbilt University’s Prompt Engineering Specialization . It's a beginner-friendly program that can help you develop skills like AI-powered creativity, verification and validation, ideation, and AI literacy. What is vibe coding? pages.text: Victory, At Last, Lesson 6 | Crash Course: American Revolution | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE CRASH COURSE Victory, At Last Lesson 6: From the battle of Monmouth to Britain’s surrender at Yorktown, Americans overcame tremendous odds to win their independence. On May 6, 1778 , George Washington’s army celebrated America’s alliance with France. Twelve days later, in British-occupied Philadelphia, musicians played “God Save the King” during a lavish tribute to the departing commander in chief, Maj. Gen. William Howe, that had fireworks and jousts between mounted officers in costume. Howe had also grown tired of the war and asked to be “relieved from this very painful service.” His successor, Lt. Gen. Henry Clinton, had orders to abandon Philadelphia and return occupying troops to New York City, thus nullifying Howe’s campaign the year before. While giving up the American capital, the British were planning to expand operations elsewhere to contend with France and target southern states. Clinton would have to hold New York while deploying troops to battle French forces in the West Indies; defend British East Florida and West Florida, which extended along the Gulf Coast to the Mississippi River; and invade Georgia and the Carolinas. Defending New York City, which the British are shown entering in 1776 in this colorized version of the original engraving (circa 1776), tied down thousands of British troops there as France entered the war against them. Introducing NPR Music's Tiny Desk (home) concerts, bringing you performances from across the country and the world. It's the same spirit — stripped-down sets, an intimate setting — just a different space. "Tiny Desk! I'm sure his fans will especially feel that sentiment since they've made a home in our social media feeds and YouTube comments for years now. We were well on the way to hosting Mac Ayres at our D.C. offices until we had to shut down and pivot. As we worked our way through the adjustment to Tiny Desk (home) concerts, he also needed some time to regroup. No over-produced beats, lots of live instruments and a stunning vocal range — and he handles all duties: guitar, bass, keyboard and background harmonies for three songs from previous albums and the premiere of a new song, "Sometimes." It’s a raw January night in the old Shetland town of Lerwick, but there’s euphoria in the air. Beside me, a man with two young children laughs as he spots a red smoky haze rising behind the town hall. “Looks like they torched the whole building,” he shouts, to grins all around. As the lord’s squad and dozens of others pour into the street, fire seethes from hundreds of torches. pages.text: Vinicius Jr: Real Madrid forward says transfer interest has affected form - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Vinicius Jr signed a new six-year contract with Real Madrid in August By Marissa Thomas BBC Sport journalist Published 16 November 2026 Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr says he felt "truly overwhelmed" by transfer speculation in the summer, which has contributed to his mixed form at the start of the season. The Brazil international has scored just once and provided three assists in 12 appearances for Jose Mourinho's side this season. He was linked with a move to Premier League champions Arsenal this summer as he entered the final year of his contract, before signing an extension at Real. The 26-year-old also says he did not train as much as he should have following Brazil's last-16 exit at the World Cup. "I don't think I prepared as well as I could have after the World Cup, because the impact of that tournament is so significant for all Brazilians," he said. "Being knocked out so early was something we hadn't expected. So, I took advantage of my holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in previous years. "That may have affected my start to the season. "On top of that, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs showing interest last summer, I felt truly overwhelmed, as with the situation at Real Madrid. But it's a very long season." May 15, 2024 Español Vision Loss and Diabetes What to know Diabetes can damage your eyes over time and cause vision loss or blindness. Managing your diabetes can help to prevent or delay eye problems. Regular eye exams help to diagnose eye problems early so you can get treatment and protect your eyesight. Diabetic retinopathy Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of blindness in working-age adults. DR is when high blood sugar damages blood vessels in the retina (a part of your eye). Damaged blood vessels can swell and leak, causing blurry vision. DR usually affects both eyes. Diabetes can damage the small blood vessels at the back of the eyes, leading to vision loss. Risk factors Anyone with type 1, type 2, or gestational diabetes (diabetes while pregnant) can develop DR. The longer you have diabetes, the more likely you are to develop it. These factors can also increase your risk: High blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels. Smoking. Being an African American, Hispanic/Latino, or American Indian or Alaska Native person. pages.text: Visit Kuélap, a Peruvian Archaeological Site a Millennium Older Than Machu Picchu | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Visit Kuélap, a Peruvian Archaeological Site a Millennium Older Than Machu Picchu The remote region north of Lima is also a paradise for lovers of mummies, wildlife, and orchids. At more than 2,500 feet, the Gocta waterfall, near the village of Cocachimba in northern Peru, is one of the world’s tallest. Ernesto Benavides By Heather Jasper Published October 20, 2026 Although the pre-Incan fortress of Kuélap is almost a thousand years older than Machu Picchu, it gets only a fraction of the crowds. The Chachapoya people built the citadel in northern Peru around the year 500 A.D. on a narrow fin of limestone high above the Utcubamba River—not unlike Machu Picchu’s perch above the Vilcanota River. Visit in 2027 to see new exhibits in the Apu Chuillaxa visitors’ center and walk a new trail in Malcapampa , an active archaeological site that has been newly opened to the public. ( See all 25 of the destinations that made our list of the best places to visit in 2027. ) When to Go The warm, rainy season arrives in the cloud forests of this part of Peru in November and lasts until April. More than a thousand orchid species are in bloom and the waterfalls thunder with extra volume. A cooler dry season from May through October offers better road conditions and drier trails, making it easier to visit archaeological sites around Kuélap. pages.description: Fat-soluble vitamins are more likely to cause adverse effects if consumed in large doses. Here’s what the experts say about vitamin A and E.
pages.text: Vitamins A and E: Why they may do more harm than good | National Geographic Fat-soluble vitamins, such as vitamin E photographed above, are stored in the body's fat reserves, which is why they have potential to accumulate to toxic levels. Photograph by Wolfgang Volz, laif/Redux Premium HEALTH How these two vitamin supplements could do more harm than good Fat-soluble vitamins are more likely to cause adverse effects if consumed in large doses. Here’s what the experts say about vitamin A and E. By Daryl Austin Last updated April 2, 2025 Vitamins and supplements are a booming industry. And while there are many important supplements that benefit people with specific deficiencies or certain health conditions, research shows and experts agree that some synthetic vitamins could cause harms such as liver damage, hair loss, joint and muscle pain, and impaired vision. "Everyone is always searching for that magic pill that will give them great health, but dietary supplements just aren't it because the benefits often don't outweigh the risks," says JoAnn Manson, chief of preventive medicine at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. ( Liver problems linked to supplement use are on the rise—here’s why .) That's not to say that some groups of people don't need to supplement certain nutrients; only that most people don't need to supplement all the vitamins they often think they do. "Generally, I don’t suggest the use of vitamin supplements unless there is a specific reason to do so," says Walter Willett, a professor of epidemiology and nutrition at Harvard T. H. Chan School

Learn about the laws and how they protect your rights and make it easier for you to vote. U.S. election laws date back to Article 1 of the Constitution. This gave states the responsibility of overseeing federal elections. Many constitutional amendments and federal laws protecting voting rights have been passed since then. Constitutional amendments affecting voting rights The 15th Amendment gave African American men the right to vote in 1870. But many weren't able to exercise this right. Some states used literacy tests and other barriers to make it harder to vote. The 19th Amendment , ratified in 1920, gave American women the right to vote. The 24th Amendment , ratified in 1964, eliminated poll taxes. The tax had been used in some states to keep African Americans from voting in federal elections. The 26th Amendment , ratified in 1971, lowered the voting age for all elections to 18. Federal voting rights laws Federal laws passed over the years help protect Americans' right to vote and make it easier for citizens to exercise that right: The Civil Rights Acts created some of the earliest federal protections against discrimination in voting. Covered nonexempt workers are entitled to a minimum wage of not less than $7.25 per hour effective July 24, 2009. Overtime pay at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate of pay is required after 40 hours of work in a workweek. FLSA Minimum Wage : The federal minimum wage is $7.25 per hour effective July 24, 2009. Many states also have minimum wage laws. In cases where an employee is subject to both state and federal minimum wage laws, the employee is entitled to the higher minimum wage. At the time of the kick-off, the All Blacks were effectively the top-ranked side in the world following South Africa's tension-filled loss to France on Friday night. So no-one gave Wales a glimmer of hope - even Warburton - with some bookmakers offering odds of 30-1 during the week. The question, not of when but can Wales beat the All Blacks again has beset them since 1953. That 73-year wait has been marred by cheating, national scandal and pure sporting drama. Little wonder then that few wanted to leave the Principality Stadium long after the final whistle had sparked unprecedented scenes of utter joy, tears and relief to the strains of Yma O Hyd. The outpouring of unbridled emotion was after a losing run - stretching across 34 matches - that has hung like a millstone around the necks of generations of Wales players. Like so many former stars, Warburton tasted success with the British & Irish Lions but lost all five meetings with New Zealand even as part of one of the most successful Wales teams of all time during the Warren Gatland era. Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff. Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953. In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins. The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes. Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time. Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back. There was ample evidence of that during Wales' remarkable 35-28 win against New Zealand last Saturday. The headline acts were the 346 tackles made by the team, which was a world record for an international match. The 38 tackles managed by lock Dafydd Jenkins matched the top individual tally, while Jac Morgan (31), James Botham (30), Eddie James (25), captain Dewi Lake (24) and Max Llewellyn (23) were not far behind. It was the impact of the bench that also proved crucial in the defensive stand of the final quarter. Steve Tandy's side ensured their place in history by ending the 73-year wait for a win against the All Blacks. Wales have won just one of their past five meetings with the Wallabies and are without a victory over them in Cardiff since 2021. But victory would complete only their second ever clean sweep of autumn internationals following the statement win on Saturday. Steve Tandy's squad came back to training on Monday, 48 hours after their famous 35-28 win saw them become the first Wales side to defeat the All Blacks since 1953. Wales had celebrated the victory on Saturday night, and the squad assembled as a whole a little later on Monday than in previous weeks as attention now turns to facing Australia this Saturday in Cardiff. There was a video shown during one of the team meetings about what the All Blacks victory meant to fans. "The players came in a bit later on Monday after being given a bit of time off to enjoy the feeling with their families," said Wales assistant coach Matt Sherratt. "We kind of reviewed the New Zealand game yesterday, but let the lads enjoy it as well. "That was powerful in terms of the reaction from friends, families and the country as a whole. "The group deserved to feel that yesterday also and we showed them what it meant to the country. "The boys loved watching some of the videos we've seen, some of the memes online about people's reactions in their living rooms. That's what it's all about." That’s not surprising given that we’re all hearing about rising rates of dementia as the population ages: A study in the January issue of Nature Medicine suggested that by the year 2060, the number of adults in the U.S. who will develop dementia is likely to double to a million people. That’s a club no one wants to join. Fortunately, science is showing that healthy eating habits can have a powerful impact on protecting cognitive function and memory . pages.text: Washington's Trials, Lesson 4 | Crash Course: American Revolution | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE CRASH COURSE Washington’s Trials Lesson 4: Defeated in New York and pursued by redcoats, a beleaguered continental army triumphed at Trenton—and revived the revolutionary cause. By the time the United States declared independence on July 4, 1776 , Washington’s army was in New York City, anticipating a British invasion. New York was home to many British loyalists, or Tories, but some had fled and others were lying low to avoid harassment by American revolutionaries. New York’s royal governor, William Tryon, had taken refuge offshore on a British sloop of war in October 1775 and plotted to assassinate Washington, a scheme exposed in June 1776 . Patriots infuriated by the plot went after suspected Tories and scourged them. One witness saw men “being carried through the streets on rails, their clothes tore from their back and their bodies pretty well mingled with the dust.” Shortly after the Declaration of Independence was read in the city, 40 colonial soldiers and sailors celebrated by hauling down a large-scale gilded lead statue of King George III on horseback at the city’s Bowling Green park, severing the head, and sending parts of the statue to Connecticut, where the metal was recast to form musket balls for Washington’s forces.
